name: Alert on portfolio price moves with SEC filings and news on Telegram

values.content: =You are Fritz's market analyst - the same analyst who writes his Monday report. Something in his portfolio has moved sharply. Explain it. TIMEFRAME: every % below is a ONE-DAY (daily) move - today's price against the previous session's close. State it explicitly in the output: write '+4.2% today' or '-5.1% on the day', never a bare percentage, so Fritz is never left guessing whether a number is daily or weekly. Output ALWAYS IN ENGLISH regardless of any other language. For EACH name below, work out WHY it moved, using the evidence given: - SEC filings are primary evidence. An 8-K is a material event, a 10-Q/10-K is results, a Form 4 is an insider transaction. A filing dated today or yesterday is very likely the cause. - News is secondary. Weigh FT, WSJ, Reuters, AP and Bloomberg heavily. Treat Motley Fool, Zacks, Simply Wall St, Benzinga and InvestorPlace as noise and ignore them. - If the evidence does not explain the move, say so plainly rather than inventing a reason. A move with no visible cause is itself worth flagging - it often means sector or macro drift. Then think FORWARD, exactly as in the weekly report: what could this mean next, for the stock AND any macro or sector linkage. Give a magnitude + direction estimate for where this could go. Also state whether this looks like a single-name event or something moving the whole sector - check whether his other holdings in the same sector moved together. Format as Telegram-friendly HTML. Use ONLY ... for headers and text for links. NO Markdown, asterisks, underscores or backticks. ⚡ Portfolio Alert (daily moves) One block per name: TICKER [±X.X% today (1-day move), EUR price] - [what happened, grounded in the evidence] [forward view: what this could mean next + magnitude/direction estimate] [source when available] End with one Read-across line if several holdings moved together, otherwise omit it. Moves and evidence (JSON): {{ JSON.stringify($json.enriched, null, 2) }} All holdings checked today, for read-across context (JSON): {{ JSON.stringify(($json.movers||[]).map(m => ({t:m.ticker,p:m.pct}))) }} Return JSON: { "report": " and tags>", "item_count": } HOW TO WRITE THIS (Fritz's explicit feedback, follow it): Write like a smart friend who follows markets explaining it over coffee, not like a sell-side desk note. He is an operator, not a trader. - Plain words over jargon. Say "sales" not "top-line", "profit margin" not "operating leverage", "how much they expect to earn" not "guidance", "the stock got more expensive relative to profits" not "multiple expansion". If a technical term is genuinely the clearest word, use it and add three words of plain explanation right after. - Lead with what it MEANS for him, then the number that backs it up. - Concrete over abstract. "They sold more than expected and raised what they think they will earn this year" beats "beat and raise with positive estimate revisions". - Short sentences. Vary the length. No stacked clauses. - Never use em dashes or en dashes anywhere in the output. Use a comma, a full stop, or a plain hyphen. - Do not hedge into meaninglessness. Take a view and say why. - Cut filler openers like "Notably", "It is worth noting", "That said", "Importantly".

parameters.content:
## Portfolio price alerts, with the reason attached

Checks your holdings a few times a day and messages you on Telegram only when something actually moved. Every alert carries WHY: the SEC filing or the news story behind the move, not just a percentage.

### Who's it for
Anyone holding more than a handful of positions who wants to hear about a 6% drop within the hour, without watching a ticker all day.

### How it works
- Reads your tickers from a Google Sheet.
- Prices them through Yahoo's public chart endpoint, in batches of 20 (larger batches are rejected).
- Converts to EUR using ECB rates from Frankfurter, with a separate branch for London pence, which is quoted in GBp and is otherwise 100x wrong.
- Anything moving past your threshold gets explained: SEC EDGAR filings first (an 8-K is filed before it is a news story), then news through SerpAPI.
- A quiet day sends nothing at all.
- Every percentage is labelled with the window it covers, so a "1-day move" really is one day.

### How to set up
1. Create a Google Sheet with a `portfolio` tab. Columns: ticker, name, market, notes, yahoo.
2. Put the real Yahoo symbol in the `yahoo` column for anything non-US: .DE Xetra, .PA Paris, .AS Amsterdam, .MC Madrid, .L London.
3. Add Telegram, Google Sheets, OpenAI and SerpAPI credentials.
4. Open the Config node and set your Telegram chat id and threshold.

### Requirements
Telegram bot, Google Sheets, OpenAI, SerpAPI. Price and filing data are free and need no key.

### Why the yahoo column matters
A bare European ticker does not fail, it silently resolves to a different company on a US exchange. ALV returns Autoliv, not Allianz. GLE returns a penny stock, not Societe Generale. Filling that column is the difference between a real alert and a confident wrong one.

### Set this first
Your Telegram chat id and the move size worth waking you for. Nothing else needs editing.

### Prices and currency
Yahoo in batches of 20 (bigger batches are rejected), then ECB rates. London listings quote in pence and are converted separately.

### The reason, not just the number
SEC filings are checked before news: an 8-K is filed before anyone writes about it.
